propositions: Removed environment variables and TOML keys currently fail silently, either redirecting the store location or downgrading security/sync/lifecycle policy gates to defaults without user awareness.
The existing deprecation registry holds only permanent aliases; removed names have no runtime signal path, leaving deprecated inputs undetectable at config discovery or CLI startup.

A dedicated RemovedInputError (BaseException subclass) raised before cache lookup and re-raised explicitly at MCP handlers ensures removed error-class inputs propagate to top-level exit and are not swallowed by try/except Exception blocks.

Setting a store/security/policy-affecting retired input must fail with a nonzero exit and a targeted message naming the old name, replacement, and removed-in release, verified by a table-driven test with no store mutation or network call.

Operationally-inert retired inputs must warn rather than error via the existing deprecation-warning channel, while genuinely-unknown keys retain the forward-compat policy (WARN/REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error).
A rebar config validate command and anti-regression golden-file CI check ensure the tombstone registry remains complete and prevent future silent removals by construction.
